case_title: Rambir v. State of NCT, Delhi
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was involved in an incident where he and his wife had a quarrel. The wife attempted to take money from his wallet, which led to a confrontation. The accused picked up a 'saria' (a type of iron rod) and used it to strangle his wife, resulting in her death. The incident occurred on the rooftop of their residence. The prosecution relied on the testimony of the accused's son, who was present at the scene, as well as other witnesses who confirmed the accused's presence and actions. The accused was initially convicted of murder under Section 302 of the IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment. However, the High Court and the Supreme Court reviewed the case, considering whether the act fell under Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC, which would reduce the charge to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II. The Supreme Court ultimately modified the conviction and imposed a sentence of 10 years' simple imprisonment.
